runs.name: Black Hills Corporation; NYSE BKH, SEC CIK 0001130464, South Dakota, 10-K filer; rate-regulated Electric Utilities (about 227,000 customers in Colorado, Montana, South Dakota and Wyoming) and Gas Utilities (about 1,138,000 customers in six states); all-stock merger with NorthWestern Energy Group signed 2025-08-18, shareholders approved 2026-04-02, regulatory approvals pending, the combined company to be renamed; Google data center agreements in Cheyenne announced 2026-10-06; the 10-K names no SEC-filing rival, NorthWestern, Avista and ONE Gas chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.box: OUT AT Q7, ON THE FLOOR AND ABOVE THE TOP OF THE RANGE
runs.entry: Price **$76.63** (close 2026-10-16, aggregator, flagged). Shares **76,253,141** on the cover of the 10-Q to 2026-06-30 (0001193125-26-337444; `Screens/cover_shares.py` agreeing; issued less treasury 76,256,336 at 2026-06-30), one class; market cap $5,843M. Sovereign **5.43%**, US Treasury 30-year par yield of 2026-10-16 (issuing authority). Read from the 10-K for 2025 (0001193125-26-046028; Items 1, 1A, 5, 7, 8), the 10-Ks for 2023, 2022, 2021 and 2018 (cash flows 2016 to 2022, Winter Storm Uri), the 10-Q to 2026-06-30, the DEF 14A of 2026-03-18 (0001193125-26-113958), the merger 8-K of 2025-08-19 (0001104659-25-080276), the 8-Ks of 2026-04-02, 2026-08-17 (NorthWestern's statements and the pro forma) and 2026-10-06 (Google data center, Cheyenne), and the merger prospectus under Rule 424(b)(3) of 2026-02-06 (0001104659-26-011554, the final S-4); operating cash 2025 $673.4M checked to the filed statement. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file. **Q1 IN**: a franchised, rate-regulated gas and electric distributor, Gas Utilities deciding at 53.2% of 2021 to 2025 segment operating income. **Q2 IN** as the regulated exception carried to Q3: the 10-K names no SEC-filing rival, NorthWestern, Avista and ONE Gas chosen as a CONVENTION of the run; return on equity 2016 to 2025 averaged 8.9% (NWE 8.5%, AVA 7.6%, OGS 8.5%), below every allowed return in the 10-K (9.30% to 10.80%). **Q3 against**: capital added 2020 to 2025 (+$2,192.7M) raised operating income $109.2M, about 5.0% pre-tax, below the bond. **Q4 accounts IN**, slightly against for featured adjusted EPS ($4.10 against GAAP $3.98) and guidance. **Q5 integrity IN**, ability slightly for. **Q6 against**: the all-stock NorthWestern merger (0.98 BKH share per NWE share, signed 2025-08-18, shareholders approved, regulatory approvals pending) gives pro forma 2025 EPS of $3.34 combined against $3.98 standalone; equity awards changed to vest in full at closing ('deviated from the original terms'); the narrower STOP tested by write-back from Q7 and not fired (BKH's price above its range). Owner cash, operating cash less stock pay, depreciation as the maintenance guess, minority distributions and book deferred tax, **$253.8M a year** 2021 to 2025, against net income to common $264.4M; the $850.0M of dividends paid while issuing $727.9M of shares and adding $754.1M of net debt. **Q7 OUT**, on the floor and above the top of the range: equity-only central (Q7, The regulated utility), debt credited $754.1M net ($930.5M gross beside), the 50.0% allowed debt share cap not binding; value range **$52.96 to $63.44 a share equity-only**, inverted (growth the bottom, the growth spending buying less than it costs); expected return 4.1% to 5.7% on every case; central growth 2.95% between the 2017 to 2020 and 2021 to 2025 averages (6.42% with 2016 beside, top $77.73, no case clears the floor either way); fair price **$28.02 equity-only, central**, **-$17.09 all-equity, not positive**, beside; the signed merger beside: range $37.34 to $54.99, fair $22.59. Q8 to Q12 not reached. Balance sheets 2016 to 2025: assets up 67%, of a $2,209M equity rise retained earnings supplied $885M, goodwill flat at $1,299.5M, debt 55.1% of capital, the $514.7M Uri regulatory asset of 2021 collected 2022 to 2025. Departures declared by the analyst: commits after each pair of questions (Q3 with Q4, Q5 with Q6), not after each question; two CONVENTIONS of the run (the book tax provision charged, the competitor choice). `tools/run.py` line d3 counts `LiabilitiesOtherThanLongtermDebtNoncurrent` ($1,523M at 2025, deferred credits and other liabilities) as debt; filed figures used, a tool defect for the operator. Contamination declared: the five latest commit subjects (BESS; the regulated-utility alerts naming AVA and OGS, two of the chosen competitors), a `Screens/_daily/` listing showing the lock, memory index lines; none used. Commits 44e3ea57 (template), 97c39b93 (Q1, Q2), 48bf3fcb (Q3, Q4), a07b74dc (Q5, Q6), 049b8f8c (Q7, Q6 write-back), 7141d07e (box, after the stop, self-audit, gaps). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_cites.py` 0 problems; the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` no missing id, 61 adjacent quoted fragments, 9 flagged and all read: filing quotes or a quote of another row standing before an id that heads the next point, **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) the regulated-utility paragraph and specific (e) do not say whether the debt credit is set against all capital spending or only the growth spending, so which product the allowed debt share caps; (2) 'the long-term debt raised over the window', gross or net; (3) aggregating the allowed debt share across jurisdictions; (4) specific (a) is written for cycles, not one-off events such as Uri; (5) growth between successive cycles is unstable and (a) meets (c); (6) Whose tax at a utility; (7) Q6's narrower STOP needs Q7's range, which comes after Q6, and the STOP omits the relative-overvaluation test **[L1997-031]**; (8) competitors when the 10-K names none; (9) the `tools/run.py` debt line. Armed at the equity-only fair price $28.02. Could not get: a maintenance and growth split of capital spending (depreciation a guess, likely short of pipe replacement); peers' allowed returns; allowed debt shares in three jurisdictions and at NorthWestern; a 2020 year-end price for the retention test's market leg.
runs.narr: Rate-regulated gas and electric distributor in eight states, gas deciding; Q1, Q2 (regulated exception), Q4, Q5 IN; Q3 against (added capital about 5.0% pre-tax, return on equity 8.9% below every allowed return); Q6 against (all-stock NorthWestern merger dilutes pro forma EPS $3.98 to $3.34, narrower STOP not fired); owner cash $253.8M a year; OUT at Q7, equity-only range $52.96 to $63.44 against $76.63, expected return 4.1% to 5.7%; fair $28.02 equity-only, -$17.09 all-equity; armed at $28.02.
